raw.title: Therapeutic Account Manager, Liver - New Orleans
raw.excerpt: MISSIONMirum Pharmaceuticals is a biopharmaceutical company dedicated to transforming the treatment of rare diseases.
raw.description:
MISSION

Mirum Pharmaceuticals is a biopharmaceutical company dedicated to transforming the treatment of rare diseases. We are passionate about advancing scientific discoveries to become important medicines for rare disease patients. We are collaborative, creative, and experienced professionals and we’re looking to augment our team with other individuals who embody our values: care, be real, get it done, and have fun, seriously.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Therapeutic Account Manager (TAM) is responsible for delivering strong, sustainable business performance and meaningful patient impact across an assigned territory. The TAM develops deep clinical and account expertise in rare cholestatic liver diseases and Mirum's Liver portfolio; identifies and prioritizes high-opportunity customers, accounts, and referral networks; and executes customized account plans that advance disease awareness, appropriate patient identification, treatment consideration, initiation, and persistence in accordance with approved indications and promotional practices.

The ideal TAM is not a transactional seller. This individual is a clinically credible, insight-led partner who engages healthcare professionals as a peer, asks thoughtful questions, constructively challenges clinical inertia, and influences change across complex accounts. The TAM works closely with the Regional Business Director and cross-functional partners to connect customer needs, patient journeys, referral pathways, access dynamics, and business opportunities while demonstrating curiosity, high emotional intelligence, resilience, ownership, and consistent follow-through.

JOB FUNCTIONS/RESPONSIBILITIES

Territory Strategy & Business Performance

  • Develop and execute a focused territory business plan aligned with national, zone, and regional priorities, with clear objectives, customer priorities, resource allocation, and measures of success.
  • Use performance data, customer insights, market intelligence, access dynamics, and competitive trends to identify opportunities, anticipate barriers, and make timely adjustments to territory strategy and execution.
  • Delivers territory business objectives through disciplined prioritization, high-quality customer engagement, effective resource stewardship, and accountability for both behaviors and results.
  • Maintain accurate and timely customer records, forecasts, expense reporting, required administrative documentation, and business updates in accordance with company expectations.

Strategic Account Management & Network Development

  • Identify, prioritize, and develop high-opportunity accounts, health systems, centers of excellence, and referral networks across pediatric and adult hepatology and gastroenterology.
  • Create and execute customized account plans that reflect the local patient journey, key stakeholders, clinical decision-making, referral patterns, access considerations, customer needs, and competitive realities.
  • Build trusted relationships with physicians, advanced practice providers, nurses, pharmacists, office staff, and other members of the care team by delivering relevant value and consistent follow-through.
  • Map influence and decision-making within complex accounts, establish clear objectives for each engagement, and secure appropriate next steps that advance the account strategy.
  • Coordinate compliant account actions across Mirum field partners, clarify ownership, and maintain momentum against agreed priorities and customer needs.

Clinical Aptitude & Customer Engagement

  • Develop and maintain deep knowledge of rare cholestatic liver disease, diagnostic pathways, mechanisms of action, clinical data, product profiles, approved uses, safety information, patient support pathways, access and reimbursement, and the evolving competitive landscape.
  • Communicate complex scientific and clinical information clearly, accurately, and credibly, tailoring the discussion to the knowledge, needs, and priorities of each healthcare professional and account.
  • Engage healthcare professionals as a clinically credible peer by asking insightful questions, listening actively, uncovering unmet needs, and connecting relevant evidence and resources to the customer's practice.
  • Execute approved promotional programs, resources, and customer engagements with consistency, clinical relevance, sound judgment, and full adherence to company policies and regulatory requirements.

Influence & Impact

  • Help customers recognize gaps in disease awareness, patient identification, referral, treatment consideration, and ongoing support by reframing issues and connecting insights across the patient journey.
  • Use high emotional intelligence, curiosity, credibility, and thoughtful questioning to build trust with skeptical, change-resistant, or highly experienced healthcare professionals.
  • Influence multiple stakeholders without authority, navigate resistance constructively, and balance persistence with judgment, empathy, and respect for customer boundaries

Customer, Patient & Caregiver Impact

  • Keep patients and caregivers at the center of territory and account decisions, with a clear understanding of the journey from disease recognition and diagnosis through treatment initiation and persistence.
  • Support a customer experience grounded in trust, empathy, responsiveness, urgency, and reliable follow-through with healthcare professionals and care teams.
  • Collaborate compliantly with Market Access and Patient Services partners to help care teams understand available resources and navigate appropriate barriers in the patient journey.
  • Identify recurring customer, access, and patient-support barriers; elevate them objectively and promptly; and partner with the appropriate internal teams to improve execution and support.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Field Insights

  • Build productive partnerships with Medical Affairs, Market Access, Patient Services, Marketing, Commercial Training and Effectiveness, Operations, Analytics, and Advocacy.
  • Work seamlessly across field roles to coordinate account strategy, align priorities, clarify responsibilities, and ensure consistent follow-through while respecting functional boundaries.
  • Capture and communicate timely, objective, and actionable field insights that can inform strategy, messaging, training, resource development, customer experience, and execution priorities.
  • Contribute actively to business reviews, training programs, team meetings, launch readiness, and cross-functional initiatives; share best practices and support the success of the broader organization.

Entrepreneurial Drive, Resilience & Culture

  • Operate with a high degree of ownership, self-motivation, resourcefulness, and initiative in an unstructured, rapidly evolving rare disease environment.
  • Create appropriate engagement opportunities in underdeveloped accounts and markets, test new approaches, learn quickly, and translate insights into action.
  • Maintain sustained drive, discipline, and performance through pressure, uncertainty, obstacles, delays, and discouragement; recover quickly and remain focused on long-term goals.
  • Demonstrate curiosity, coachability, and a commitment to continuous learning; actively seek feedback and apply coaching to strengthen clinical, strategic, and selling capabilities.
  • Model Mirum's values and the highest standards of ethical conduct, compliance, transparency, inclusion, and respect in every internal and external interaction.

QUALIFICATIONS

Education/Experience:

  • Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree preferred.
  • 5+ years of progressive sales experience in the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry.
  • Demonstrated track record of consistently delivering business results in a complex specialty, rare disease, orphan drug, or high-science market.
  • Rare disease experience is highly preferred; experience in hepatology, gastroenterology, pediatric specialty care, or another complex specialty market is highly desirable.
  • Strong clinical aptitude and demonstrated ability to learn, retain, and communicate complex disease-state, diagnostic, mechanism-of-action, clinical-data, and product information.
  • Experience with account-based selling across health systems, centers of excellence, multidisciplinary care teams, referral networks, and influential healthcare professionals.
  • Demonstrated ability to use insight-led or challenger-style selling to constructively challenge the status quo, influence behavior, and advance customer decision-making.
  • Working knowledge of access and reimbursement dynamics, patient support pathways, and the role of patient services in rare disease markets.
  • Strong business acumen and ability to interpret performance data, identify insights, develop territory and account strategies, and translate plans into consistent field execution.
  • Exceptional interpersonal skills, emotional intelligence, communication, presentation, judgment, and ability to build trust with diverse and highly sophisticated customers.
  • Proven self-motivation, resourcefulness, resilience, organization, and ability to prioritize and perform independently in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment.
  • Demonstrated success partnering cross-functionally with Medical Affairs, Market Access, Patient Services, Marketing, Commercial Training and Effectiveness, Operations, and Analytics.
  • Commitment to ethical conduct, compliance, and approved promotional practices, with sound judgment in complex customer and patient-related situations.
  • Valid driver's license and ability to travel up to 70%, including frequent overnight travel and occasional weekend commitments.

Mirum Pharmaceuticals is committed to Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) and to compliance with all Federal, State and Local laws that prohibit employment discrimination on the basis of race, age, national origin, ethnicity, religion, gender, gender identity, pregnancy, marital status, sexual orientation, citizenship, genetic disposition or characteristics, disability, veteran’s status or any other classification protected by applicable State/Federal/Local laws.

Mirum Pharmaceuticals provides reasonable accommodation for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in job application procedures.

raw.description:
Workforce Classification:

Telecommuter

Join Our Team: Do Meaningful Work and Improve People’s Lives

Our purpose, to improve customers’ lives by making healthcare work better, is far from ordinary. And so are our employees. Working at Premera means you have the opportunity to drive real change by transforming healthcare.

Premera is committed to being a workplace where people feel empowered to grow, innovate, and lead with purpose. By investing in our employees and fostering a culture of collaboration and continuous development, we’re able to better serve our customers. It’s this commitment that has earned us recognition as one of the best companies to work for. Learn more about our recent awards and recognitions as a greatest workplace.

Learn how Premera supports our members, customers and the communities that we serve through our Healthsource blog: .

The Instructional Designer designs and develops learning content and business process documentation that support Premera’s purpose, values and business initiatives. The incumbent will collaborate with subject matter experts to develop instructional content including participant workbooks, facilitator guides, PowerPoint decks, classroom activities, job aids, evaluation tools and business process documentation using adult learning theory for instructor-led and e-learning training.

What you will do:

  • Design and develop instructor-led & computer-based training material using adult learning theory and instructional design methodologies to support blended delivery of training and documentation.
  • Design, develop or select course content, such as participant workbooks, facilitator guides, PowerPoint decks, classroom activities, job aids, eLearning scripts, business process documentation, and evaluation tools for instructor-led courses.
  • Support multiple projects by meeting project timelines and deliverables; supporting project plan development and providing project progress updates.
  • Participate in instructional analysis: determine knowledge, skills, attitudes, competencies required and gaps in learning and business process documentation; assess effectiveness and efficiency of materials including ease of instructional use and student learning, knowledge transfer, and satisfaction.
  • Collaborate with team to write performance/behavioral objectives, determine appropriate learning solutions based upon established learning objectives; analyze relevant learning situations to determine appropriate training solutions applying appropriate learning theories and design principles; develop criterion-based assessments and performance measures.
  • Consult and collaborate with internal business partners to develop appropriate training or business process documentation.
  • Interview subject matter experts or conduct other research to develop instructional content.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What you will bring:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in curriculum development, education, organizational development, instructional design, or technical writing or four years of work experience. (Required)
  • Two (2) years’ experience writing business process, designing instructor-led and web-based curriculum including scripts and facilitator guides, conducting business needs analyses and familiarity with Camtasia and Articulate Storyline software. (Required)
  • Industry certifications in instructional design, curriculum development, technical writing, or content-specific certifications, as appropriate. (Preferred)
  • Experience with learning management system (LMS) architecture and deployment in a corporate learning environment. (Preferred)

What you will gain:

  • Experience designing engaging instructor-led and e-learning content.
  • Stronger skills in adult learning and instructional design.
  • Collaboration with subject matter experts and business partners.
  • Exposure to diverse learning tools, projects, and documentation.
  • Opportunities to measure and improve training effectiveness.

Physical Requirements:
The following have been identified as essential physical requirements of this job and must be performed with or without an accommodation: This is primarily a sedentary role which requires the ability to exert up to 10 lbs. of force occasionally and/or a negligible amount of force frequently or constantly to lift, carry, push, pull, or otherwise move objects, including the human body.

This role requires the ability to keyboard and to communicate clearly and understandably in person and over the telephone.

Premera total rewards

Our comprehensive total rewards package provides support, resources, and opportunities to help employees thrive and grow. Our total rewards are more than a collection of perks, they're a reflection of our commitment to your health and well-being. We offer a broad array of rewards including physical, financial, emotional, and community benefits, including:

  • Medical, vision, and dental coverage with low employee premiums.

  • Voluntary benefit offerings, including pet insurance for paw parents.

  • Life and disability insurance.

  • Retirement programs, including a 401K employer match and, believe it or not, a pension plan that is vested after 3 years of service.

  • Wellness incentives with a wide range of mental well-being resources for you and your dependents, including counseling services, stress management programs, and mindfulness programs, just to name a few.

  • Generous paid time off to reenergize.

  • Looking for continuing education? We have tuition assistance for both undergraduate and graduate degrees.

  • Employee recognition program to celebrate anniversaries, team accomplishments, and more.

For our hybrid employees, our on-campus model provides flexibility to create your own routine with access to on-site resources, networking opportunities, and team engagement.

  • Commuter perks make your trip to work less impactful on the environment and your wallet.

  • Free convenient on-site parking.

  • Subsidized on-campus cafes make lunchtime connections with colleagues fun and affordable.

  • Participate in engaging on-site activities such as health and wellness events, coffee connects, disaster preparedness fairs and more.

  • Our complementary fitness & well-being center offers both in-person and virtual workouts and nutritional counseling.

  • Need a brain break? Challenge someone to a game of shuffleboard or ping pong while on campus.

Equal employment opportunity/affirmative action:

Premera is an equal opportunity/affirmative action employer. Premera seeks to attract and retain the most qualified individuals without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, marital status, veteran status, gender or gender identity, sexual orientation, genetic information or any other protected characteristic under applicable law.

If you need an accommodation to apply online for positions at Premera, please contact Premera Human Resources via email at or via phone at 425-918-4785.

Overview

As the Learning & Capacity Building Coordinator, you will strengthen the capacity of partner organizations participating in a U.S. Government-funded humanitarian response and disaster preparedness program. Through capacity assessments, coaching, learning initiatives, and partner support, you will help organizations build the knowledge, skills, systems, and practices needed to better serve vulnerable children and communities affected by crises.

Working closely with the prime award recipient, subaward partners, subject matter experts, and program teams, you will coordinate and support learning and capacity-strengthening activities, monitor progress, and promote knowledge sharing and continuous improvement across the consortium.

What will you do?

  • Maintain a personal relationship with Jesus Christ. Be a consistent witness for Jesus Christ, maintaining a courteous, Christ-like attitude in dealing with people within and outside of Compassion, and faithfully uphold Compassion’s ministry in prayer.

  • Act as an advocate to raise the awareness of the needs of children. Understand Christ’s mandate to protect children. Commit to and prioritizes child protection considerations in all decision-making, tasks and activities across the ministry. Abide by all behavioral expectations in Compassion’s Statement of Commitment to Child Protection and Code of Conduct. Report any concerns of abuse, neglect or exploitation of children through Compassion’s internal reporting process and appropriately support responses to incidents if they occur.

  • Uphold and engage in Compassion’s core Cultural Behaviors.

  • Coordinate learning and capacity-building activities that support grant objectives and program outcomes.

  • Provide humanitarian sector coaching for New and Underutilized Partners (NUPs) and recommend suitable operational engagements.

  • Collaborate with subject matter experts and stakeholders to identify learning needs and develop effective training and capacity-strengthening solutions.

  • Design and develop learning materials, including curricula, facilitator guides, participant resources, job aids, and digital learning content.

  • Coordinate the delivery of instructor-led, virtual, blended, and self-paced learning programs.

  • Support training logistics, scheduling, communications, participant engagement, and learning documentation.

  • Apply adult learning principles and instructional design best practices to create engaging and effective learning experiences.

  • Monitor and evaluate learning activities to assess effectiveness, identify improvements, and measure outcomes.

  • Maintain learning resources and knowledge management systems to ensure accessibility and consistency.

  • Support partner and staff capacity development through coaching, resource development, and technical assistance.

  • Contribute to grant reporting, work planning, and documentation related to learning and capacity-building activities.

  • Foster collaboration and knowledge sharing across teams, partners, and stakeholders.

  • Stay informed of emerging trends, tools, and best practices in learning, capacity development, emergency preparedness, and humanitarian programming.

What do you bring?

  • Bachelor's degree in a related field

  • 7+ years of relevant work experience

  • Experience in humanitarian and disaster relief program design, management and accountability will be valuable in assessing gaps, conducting coaching sessions and applying capacity development plans.

  • Experience supporting donor-funded, humanitarian, emergency preparedness, international development, or related programs preferred.

  • Proven experience designing and delivering field-based, hands-on learning, training, and capacity-building initiatives.

  • Demonstrated ability to coordinate multiple projects and stakeholders while managing competing priorities.

  • Strong communication, facilitation, and relationship-building skills.

  • Exceptional written and verbal English communication skills are required. Bilingual or multilingual proficiency in French and/or Spanish is preferred.

Why work here?

  • The mission: Join a team that is motivated to release children from poverty in Jesus’ name.

raw.description:
We're so happy you're here! Thank you for checking our job out and we hope to have the chance to meet you in our interview process!

About the role

We are hiring for our first dedicated international quality hire at Grüns. You'll own the quality system for every market outside the US: product release, specifications, complaints and adverse events, incident management, contract manufacturer oversight, stability, and transit qualification. For products sold in the EU, you'll build and run the Quality Management System processes that keep us compliant with EU and local market requirements across the product lifecycle.

Today these responsibilities sit informally with the US QA team. The job is to figure out where they should live, build the processes, and then run them. You'll work across Regulatory, Supply Chain, Operations, and our external manufacturing and 3PL partners, and you'll be the escalation point when something goes wrong in an international market.

Location:

While this role is part of our global remote HQ, we feel a candidate based in or around Germany or the United Kingdom will be most successful in this role.

The team members you’ll be working with most are in multiple countries and time zones, so we ask that you are comfortable working a way that allows for some overlap in working hours to collaborate.

More generally, we operate in a fully remote, high trust environment with teammates across multiple countries and time zones. While we work async by default, we come together in person twice a year for offsites that help us connect, align, and build real relationships IRL.

In this role, you will:

  • Release finished products only after verifying specs, COAs, manufacturing docs, deviations, and market-specific requirements
  • Own consumer complaint intake and triage across level 1, 2, and 3
  • Build and run traceability, recall/withdrawal, mock recall, complaint, adverse-event, and food safety incident processes for EU products
  • Own supplier and contract manufacturer qualification: Quality Agreements, audits, CAPAs/SCARs, deviations, change controls, investigations, ongoing performance monitoring
  • Run BMT testing and oversee microbiological, chemical, allergen, contaminant, nutritional, and stability testing, including OOS/OOT investigations and third-party labs
  • Assess quality and regulatory risk on any formulation, ingredient, supplier, process, spec, packaging, or labeling change before it ships. Even a packaging color update can get held at customs in markets like China without sign-off
  • Partner with Regulatory Affairs to keep formulations, specs, labels, claims, and packaging compliant by market
  • Own quality oversight of international manufacturing, packaging, warehousing, and distribution partners, including 3PLs
  • Set and monitor international quality KPIs and keep us audit-ready

We're looking for someone who:

  • Has a minimum of 5 years of quality assurance experience in food, beverage, dietary supplement, or consumer health, with meaningful time spent on products sold outside the US
  • Has hands-on EU and international quality experience. You've managed quality processes for food, dietary supplement, or consumer health products sold in the EU and across multiple regulatory jurisdictions, and you understand how quality and regulatory requirements differ by market
  • Has working knowledge of EU food and food supplement quality requirements, including GMP and food safety requirements, HACCP, traceability and recall, allergen management, specifications, supplier and contract manufacturer controls, analytical testing, stability, change control, product release, and labeling and claims oversight. Experience across multiple EU member states is a strong plus
  • Has real depth in core quality systems: you've owned CAPAs, investigations, root cause analysis, specification creation, document control, and change control, not just participated in them
  • Has qualified, audited, and managed external manufacturers and co-packers, and held them to account
  • Has owned or contributed materially to a recall, withdrawal, or market action, and knows what good looks like under pressure
  • Is comfortable owning stability protocols and managing third-party labs
  • Can work across US, UK/EU, and Asia time zones with a distributed team and external partners

Approach to the role:

  • You treat documentation as protection, not paperwork
  • You catch the small stuff, like a packaging color change, before it turns into a blocked shipment
  • You build with scale in mind, since we're small today and growing internationally fast
  • You bring high ownership and don't need to be micromanaged to move fast

Compensation & Benefits:

At Grüns, we are committed to offering a competitive total compensation package grounded in market data and aligned to our size, stage, industry, and geographic location. Compensation for this role will be benchmarked to the local market and may vary based on experience and country of hire. In addition to base compensation roles include a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance.

A bit about us...

At Grüns, we believe that foundational nutrition should be simple and convenient for everyone. We're dedicated to bringing comprehensive and real nutrition to you through our gummies, formulated from 60 nutrient-dense and whole-food ingredients. Simply enjoy a grab-and-go snack pack of gummies daily whenever fits best in your schedule and wherever life takes you.

Like you, we were disappointed. There’s an infinite number of “nutrition” companies, all focused on what’s best for them — not what’s best for you. Hundreds of products to sell you on, low-quality ingredients, and small nutrient doses. We’ve seen it all.

So we decided it was time to fix it. No more choking on and popping pills like a pharmacy. No more clean-up and disgust from gross powders. And no more cobbling together handfuls to dozens of supplements. Grüns is comprehensive nutrition, made convenient and delicious.

What we care about...

Be the Best: We hold ourselves, our teams, and our partners to an incredibly high standard - and we raise the bar constantly. "We've never done this before" isn't an excuse here. It's an invitation.

Own It: We act like our name is on the door. That means taking complete ownership of outcomes, collaborating deeply, working through roadblocks - not around them - and never waiting for someone else to solve the problem. Great owners are great partners.

Drive Impact, Urgently: We measure impact, not effort. We work smart and hard, move fast, and use every tool at our disposal - including AI - to focus our energy where it matters most.

Compensation & Perks:

For every role, we aim to have highly competitive compensation and opportunity for impact and career growth.

Everyone at Grüns works hard, but we believe in wellness and balance too. We have super strong benefits coverage -- for you and your family, generous PTO, free Grüns, and a few more perks centered around health and well-being that we can't wait to tell you about!

Reporting directly to the CFO, you will have full responsibility for the General Ledger, lead the transition from an outside accounting firm to a fully in-house accounting function, manage monthly close and reconciliations, prepare financial reporting, and oversee the Accounts Payable and Accounts Receivable team.
QuickBooks expertise is essential for this position. This role requires more than day-to-day usage. You must be comfortable configuring and optimizing QuickBooks and have experience with QuickBooks implementations.
This is a hands-on position for someone who is highly accurate, independent, comfortable working in a fast-paced remote environment, and willing to support operational responsibilities beyond traditional accounting when needed.
Why This Opportunity?
  • Take full ownership of the company's accounting operations and General Ledger.
  • Become the internal QuickBooks expert for the organization.
  • Work directly with the CFO and play a key role in strengthening the finance function.
  • Lead the transition from outsourced accounting to a fully in-house operation.
  • Manage and improve accounting processes, controls, and reporting.
  • Work remotely with significant autonomy and responsibility.
What You'll Do
QuickBooks & General Ledger
  • Configure and optimize QuickBooks to support the company's accounting structure and reporting requirements.
  • Lead or support QuickBooks configuration and implementation initiatives.
  • Lead the transition of the General Ledger from an outside accounting firm to an in-house function.
  • Maintain, reconcile, and close the books monthly.
  • Establish and maintain the Chart of Accounts and appropriate classification standards.
Financial Reporting & Cash Management
  • Prepare accurate financial statements across the company's business divisions.
  • Prepare and review Profit & Loss (P&L) statements.
  • Oversee bank reconciliations.
  • Monitor the company's cash position.
  • Maintain accurate and reliable financial information for CFO review.
Team Leadership & Client Support
  • Supervise Accounts Receivable and Accounts Payable specialists.
  • Review and approve invoices, hours reports, and client statements before distribution.
  • Review and approve payroll, vendor payments, and expense submissions.
  • Interface with clients regarding accounting-related requests when required.
  • Ensure accounting work completed by the team meets established standards.
  • Support operational and non-accounting matters that may arise within a small-team environment.
Tax & Accounting Controls
  • Coordinate payroll tax, sales tax, and 1099-related matters.
  • Execute accounting policies established by the CFO accurately and consistently.
  • Maintain strong accounting controls and a high standard of accuracy.
Qualifications
Required Qualifications
  • Prior experience as a Financial Controller, Senior Accountant, or similar senior accounting professional with full ownership of the General Ledger.
  • Advanced, hands-on QuickBooks expertise.
  • Professional experience with QuickBooks Online and/or QuickBooks Desktop.
  • Experience configuring QuickBooks and/or leading a QuickBooks implementation.
  • Strong experience managing the General Ledger, reconciliations, and month-end close.
  • Experience preparing financial statements and P&L reports.
  • Strong understanding of Chart of Accounts structures and accounting classifications.
  • Experience overseeing or working closely with Accounts Payable and Accounts Receivable.
  • Strong attention to detail and consistently low error rates.
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision.
  • Ability to execute accounting policies and procedures with precision.
  • Comfortable supporting operational responsibilities beyond traditional accounting.
  • C1/C2 English proficiency, both written and spoken.
  • Ability to work with required overlap during U.S. business hours.
Preferred Qualifications
  • Experience transitioning an accounting function from an external accounting firm to an in-house team.
  • Experience with BigTime or similar project accounting software.
  • Previous experience in professional services, interior design, architecture, construction, or project-based businesses.
  • Experience supervising accounting or bookkeeping professionals.
How Success Is Measured
Success in this position will be measured by your ability to:
  • Maintain an accurate and reliable General Ledger.
  • Independently execute reconciliations and month-end close.
  • Configure and optimize QuickBooks according to business requirements.
  • Successfully support the transition to an in-house accounting function.
  • Deliver accurate and timely financial reporting.
  • Maintain strong accounting controls and a consistently low error rate.
  • Effectively oversee AP and AR activities.
  • Work independently while executing CFO policies accurately.
  • Communicate professionally with U.S.-based colleagues and clients.
Video Presentation Required
As part of your application, please submit a short video in English introducing yourself and briefly summarizing your accounting background, followed by a 30-second to 1-minute overview of your QuickBooks experience, including how many years you have used it professionally, whether you have worked with QuickBooks Online and/or Desktop, your main responsibilities in the system, and any experience configuring QuickBooks or leading an implementation.
Why Join Us?
  • $2,000 – $4,000 USD/month, based on experience and location.
  • Fully remote work environment.
  • Direct exposure to the CFO and company leadership.
  • Significant ownership of the accounting function.
  • Opportunity to lead an important financial operations transition.
  • Long-term, full-time contractor opportunity.
  • Short initial trial period to ensure mutual fit.
Important Notes
Advanced QuickBooks expertise is a core requirement for this position. Basic familiarity, occasional use, or self-taught exposure without substantial professional experience will not be sufficient.
Candidates should be prepared to clearly explain their years of QuickBooks experience, versions used, responsibilities within the system, experience running monthly close, and any QuickBooks configuration or implementation experience.
C1/C2 English is mandatory. The role operates entirely in English with a U.S.-based team and, at times, directly with clients.
This is a permanent, full-time contractor opportunity with a short initial trial period.

This is a remote/telecommute position.

RethinkCare is the first and only human- and web-based program to provide effective & affordable clinical best practice tools to support multiple populations within the neurodiversity community: employees caring for children/teens with learning and behavioral needs, neurodivergent employees, and the managers and organizations that support them. Developed by internationally recognized clinicians and leaders, Rethink empowers employees to pursue individualized skill-building and support both online and through 1:1 consultations, thus, reducing stress, creating a nurturing environment, and increasing productivity at work.

Job Description / Key Responsibilities

The Clinical and Family Services Director – (Mandarin-speaking) BCBA primary responsibility is to conduct 1:1 teleconsultation services (over phone or video chat) across two distinct teams:

  1. A parent training program, consisting of parents and caregivers raising children with various learning and behavioral needs

  1. A neurodiversity at work program, consisting of both neurodivergent professionals and/or their managers

The Director will put emphasis on the ongoing nature of consultation and strive to ensure regular follow-ups with the client are achieved. They will log notes, recommendations, referrals, and respond to client messages within 1 business day.

This role includes providing guidance and education around:

  • Behavior analytic tips and strategies to implement in the home/community (e.g., potty training, social skills, advocacy skills, activities of daily living, etc.)

  • The school system/IEP process/transition to adulthood programming

  • Navigating diagnoses, disclosure, self-advocacy, and building executive functioning skills in the workplace

  • Referrals to other company-sponsored benefits when appropriate (EAP, health plan, etc.)

They will report to the Senior Director of Clinical Services and acts as the ultimate advocate for parents.

  • Board Certified Behavior Analyst or international equivalent

  • Minimum 5 years working directly with individuals with developmental disabilities utilizing ABA principles (add’l experience with learning disabilities, counseling, and/or supporting adults in the workplace is a plus)
  • Minimum 5 years conducting parent training utilizing ABA principles
  • Experience supporting neurodivergent professionals (e.g., ADHD and Level 1 autism) in the workplace

  • Ability to work independently with minimal day-to-day supervision and take initiative
  • Ability to make independent decisions and communicate accordingly
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and security of vital project/client information
  • Ability to work on a multi-disciplinary team to connect, remotely, with colleagues of all professional backgrounds

  • Bilingual in Italian, and ability to work international time zones, strongly preferred

raw.description:
“In 36 months, agentic AI systems will be an operating reality across major institutions. We intend to be central to it.” — Dr. Jim Rebesco, Cofounder and CEO, Striveworks

The government’s demand for AI is growing far faster than the systems required to support it. Fewer than 15% of federal AI programs have reached sustained production, despite billions of dollars invested. The models perform in testing, but they degrade in the real world. And when performance drops, trust goes with it.

Striveworks was built to solve that problem.

What you’ll build

Since 2018, we have delivered the most trusted AI systems operating in real-world use cases—providing a layer of assurance underneath hundreds of deployed models that monitors performance, manages drift, and sustains systems long after they leave the lab.

As Product Marketing Manager, you will own the collateral that carries our products into every sales conversation, evaluation, and briefing across our AI operations (AIOps) platform, agentic AI orchestrator, and vertical solutions. You will work closely with our product managers, data scientists, and sales team to turn technical substance into collateral that is accurate, compelling, and appropriate for audiences ranging from technical evaluators to senior government decision-makers.

Your day-to-day will include:

  • Owning the collateral library: Maintain a complete, current, and organized library of sales and technical collateral across all products. Identify gaps and drive them to closure.
  • Turning technical input into finished collateral: Work with the PM for each product area to gather technical facts and rough outlines. Independently produce refined presentations and accompanying graphics/diagrams, proactively asking the right questions to fill gaps rather than waiting to be fully briefed.
  • Keeping messaging aligned: Partner closely with the Communications department to ensure that product messaging and collateral align with Striveworks’ broader narratives, voice, and audience dynamics. Support Communications as needed by adapting and developing product content and collateral for different audiences and uses.
  • Supporting event and conference operations: Assist in orchestrating our presence at industry and government conferences, including attendance planning, registration, and booth setup/breakdown, ensuring collateral and messaging are current and conference-ready.
  • Growing into technical content: Partner with product managers, data scientists, and technical teams to produce broader technical content, starting with blog posts.
  • Staying ahead of the curve: Track customer feedback, market trends, competitive capabilities, and emerging technologies to keep collateral and messaging current.

What it’s like here

We lead with trust, treat each other with respect, and use candor consistently, kindly, and constructively. We care deeply about our work, and we find genuine satisfaction in doing it well. Above all, we take ownership—because we feel the weight of collective results personally. We are looking for people who share these values and are eager to put them into practice.

What we’re looking for

  • A bachelor’s degree, or equivalent experience, in a technical, communications, or related field
  • 6+ years of product marketing, sales enablement, or technical marketing experience, preferably for enterprise, government, or technical B2B products
  • The ability to understand AI/machine learning, AIOps, and agentic/orchestration concepts well enough to ask sharp questions of product managers and data scientists and represent our products credibly
  • A strong portfolio of written and visual collateral: decks, one-pagers, briefs, or similar assets
  • A proven ability to turn rough, incomplete technical input into polished, decision-ready output with minimal back-and-forth
  • Experience partnering closely with product and technical teams to source accurate content
  • The ability to communicate technical concepts and value propositions to both technical and non-technical senior audiences
  • Strong organizational skills—able to own and maintain a growing collateral library without things going stale
  • A self-starter mindset: comfortable identifying gaps and driving them to closure without heavy direction
  • Due to the nature of this role, candidates must be a US person (a US citizen, a US national, or a Green Card holder)

The following isn’t required, but we’d love to see it:

  • Experience marketing to public-sector, defense, or other mission-driven government buyers
  • Prior experience as a product manager, data scientist, ML engineer, or solutions architect
  • Proficiency with design tools (e.g., Figma, Adobe Creative Suite) to build polished graphics and diagrams
  • Experience producing technical content such as blog posts, case studies, or tutorials

This position offers a fully remote work environment, or you can work hybrid/on site at our office in Austin, TX. You will be expected to travel up to 20% of the time.

Compensation

The anticipated base pay range for this position is $145,000–$195,000/year. Striveworks’ total compensation package includes a competitive base salary, equity grants, and cash bonuses.

Benefits include:

  • Medical/dental/vision insurance
  • Voluntary life, long-term disability, accident, and hospital indemnity insurance
  • HSA and FSA (including dependent care FSA) plans
  • 401(k) plan
  • Unlimited PTO
  • Paid parental leave

Ready to build systems that work for a mission that matters? Let’s talk.

Striveworks is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate in employment on the basis of race, color, religion, belief, sex (including pregnancy and gender identity or expression), national origin, social or ethnic origin, political affiliation, sexual orientation, marital status, disability, genetic information, age, membership in an employee organization, retaliation, parental status, military service, or other non-merit factors. Striveworks will not tolerate discrimination or harassment of any kind.

If you require assistance or a reasonable accommodation in the application process, please contact People Operations at .

raw.description:
What you will do:

As an independent contractor, you will be working from home as a freelance transcriptionist and translator, making an accurate text document of the contents of audio, video, typed or handwritten material.

We transcribe oral history interviews (with WWII veterans, women in academia, farmers, midwives…), focus groups, financial forecasts or quarterly reports, tech webinars, commencement addresses, interviews about NGO work, educational reform or health care access, or anything else you could think of, and even occasionally TV shows. We don't do medical transcription.

Who we’re looking for:

  • U.S. Citizens or U.S. Resident Alien as described on IRS form W-9.
  • Bilingual transcriptionists/translators of Spanish and English.
  • Fast and accurate typists (minimum of 80 wpm), who can deliver files on deadline without question.
  • People with a wide range of interests or educational experiences. As the subject matter varies broadly, it’s easier to understand the flow of conversation when you have some context for what is being discussed.

Requirements

  • Strong language, style, and punctuation skills, and the capability and willingness to follow our transcription style manual as well as project-specific instructions.
  • Ability to verify names and terms via brief internet research. Much of the work we do is for archives, so these transcripts will become part of a historical record and need to be of high quality to reflect that permanence.

What you will need

  • A reliable internet connection is a must. ATC sends project files via Dropbox links, so no special FTP setup is necessary.
  • For confidentiality reasons, we require that you use an email address that no one else has access to.
  • Transcripts should be returned to ATC as .doc files. You are not strictly required to use Microsoft Word; you can also use Open Office or some other program that has the capability to save as a .doc file as long as the formatting requirements are met and the functionality of the end product is indistinguishable from a document completed in Word.
  • ATC highly recommends the use of transcription software (such as ExpressScribe) controlled via hotkeys or a foot pedal, and the use of good-quality headphones to cut down on ambient noise while you are transcribing.

How do I get hired as a freelance transcriptionist?

No calls, please. File your online application here and include:

  • Current resume (PDF)
  • Cover letter (PDF)
  • A screenshot of the results from a three-minute typing test on www.typingtest.com (our minimum requirement is 80 wpm with 98% accuracy)

raw.description:
About Engine

Engine is the all-in-one travel and spend management platform trusted by 38K+ businesses and groups representing 1.8M+ travelers. We're the retailer and the rails of business travel, the fastest-growing company in travel tech, built on a decade of proprietary technology, supply, and pricing no one else can replicate. Other travel and AI companies run on our infrastructure to book real trips, hold rates, and move payments, without building any of it themselves. We built it, AI-forward at every layer, from how travelers book to how the rails run.

That work has earned recognition as one of Fast Company's Best Workplaces for Innovators (2025), TravelTech's Reservation Platform of the Year (2026), and one of Built In's Best Places to Work (2020–2026).

We're looking for bold, ambitious people to help redefine how businesses manage and experience travel. Working here, you can expect exponential growth, an ambitious pace, full ownership, and high-caliber colleagues who push you to do the best work of your career. Every hire raises the bar.

Come outpace the ordinary and build the future of travel with us.

As a Sr. ARC Specialist, you will play a critical role in maintaining the accuracy, integrity, and efficiency of all airline ticketing and financial reporting processes. Sitting at the intersection of Flight Operations, Finance, and Member Support, you will be directly responsible for managing ARC (Airlines Reporting Corporation) processes, ensuring regulatory adherence, and driving excellence across all air travel transactions.

This high-impact role requires a deep understanding of airline ticketing — including exchanges, refunds, and voids — as well as expert-level knowledge of ARC procedures, GDS platforms, and reconciliation workflows. You will serve as the final authority on transaction accuracy and compliance, overseeing end-to-end settlement cycles, resolving discrepancies, and implementing scalable SOPs to support sustainable growth.

This role is ideal for someone who thrives in a fast-paced environment, brings meticulous attention to detail, and is passionate about upholding the highest standards.

Your Mission:

As part of the Engine team, you’ll play a vital role in an environment where innovation meets collaboration. Here’s what you’ll take charge of:

ARC Settlement and Financial Reconciliation

  • Own and manage the full ARC settlement process on a weekly basis, including submission, reconciliation, and payment via Back Office Systems, and IAR.
  • Process and reconcile all transactions—sales, exchanges, refunds, voids, commissions, TASFs—across Amadeus GDS, ARC, and financial platforms.
  • Work with Finance to authorize and process the weekly cash remit draft to ARC, ensuring regulatory compliance and timely payments.
  • Perform daily balancing of ARC transactions, resolving discrepancies in coordination with ticketing and accounting teams.

Ticketing Audit and Debit Memo Management

  • Review issued airline tickets, ensuring accuracy in complex transactions like refunds, exchanges, MCOs, and fare rule applications.
  • Lead the end-to-end Debit Memo (ADM) management process, including daily monitoring of ARC Memo Manager, dispute resolution, chargebacks, trend analysis, and financial reporting.
  • Identify root causes of debit memo violations and implement corrective actions in partnership with operations and finance.
  • Support internal and external audits with complete, audit-ready documentation related to ARC reporting and ticketing activities.

Compliance, Process Improvement, and Cross-Functional Support

  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to maintain and continuously improve Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to ensure compliance, accuracy, and efficiency in ticketing and settlement workflows and address any financial or system interface issues.
    Provide ongoing guidance and training on ARC policy updates, TRAMS/IAR usage, and best practices in ticketing compliance.

Industry Knowledge and Continuous Learning

  • Stay abreast of ARC regulations, airline policy updates, and travel industry developments, communicating relevant impacts to internal stakeholders.
  • Assist with the testing, implementation, and maintenance of back-office system updates and integrations.

What You’ll Bring to Engine:

We’re looking for someone who’s ready to make an impact and grow alongside us:

  • Minimum 5 years of hands-on experience in ARC reporting, reconciliation, and settlement in a high-volume TMC, OTA or travel agency environment.
  • Expert-level proficiency with Amadeus GDS and NDC technology.
  • Deep knowledge of ARC processes, IAR, and back-office systems.
  • ARC Specialist certification, or ability to obtain within 30 days of hire.
  • Possess expert-level knowledge of advanced fare rules, intricate fare construction, commission structures, exchanges, and refunds.
  • Proven ability to research, analyze, and resolve financial and transactional discrepancies.
  • High attention to detail with exceptional accuracy in data handling and reporting.
  • Proficiency in Google Workspace and other financial and reporting applications
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with strong negotiation and documentation abilities.

Compensation
Our compensation packages are based on several factors, including your experience, expertise, and location. In addition to a competitive base salary, all roles receive equity. Depending on the role, total compensation may also include an annual bonus. Your recruiter will share your complete compensation package as you move through the process.

Base Pay Range
$65,000—$90,000 USD

The Engine Edge: Perks & Compensation
We believe in rewarding great work with great benefits:

  • Compensation: Competitive base pay tied to role and experience, with equity for all employees. Some roles are also eligible for bonuses or commissions.
  • Benefits: Check out our full list at
  • Environments for Success: Different roles have different needs in terms of the environments that drive success which is why we have a hybrid-hub model. Whether you are in one of our amazing offices or fully remote, we'll make sure you have what you need to succeed.

Perks and benefits may vary based on employment type, location, and more

raw.title: Therapeutic Account Manager, Liver - Manchester
raw.excerpt: MISSIONMirum Pharmaceuticals is a biopharmaceutical company dedicated to transforming the treatment of rare diseases.
raw.description:
MISSION

Mirum Pharmaceuticals is a biopharmaceutical company dedicated to transforming the treatment of rare diseases. We are passionate about advancing scientific discoveries to become important medicines for rare disease patients. We are collaborative, creative, and experienced professionals and we’re looking to augment our team with other individuals who embody our values: care, be real, get it done, and have fun, seriously.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Therapeutic Account Manager (TAM) is responsible for delivering strong, sustainable business performance and meaningful patient impact across an assigned territory. The TAM develops deep clinical and account expertise in rare cholestatic liver diseases and Mirum's Liver portfolio; identifies and prioritizes high-opportunity customers, accounts, and referral networks; and executes customized account plans that advance disease awareness, appropriate patient identification, treatment consideration, initiation, and persistence in accordance with approved indications and promotional practices.

The ideal TAM is not a transactional seller. This individual is a clinically credible, insight-led partner who engages healthcare professionals as a peer, asks thoughtful questions, constructively challenges clinical inertia, and influences change across complex accounts. The TAM works closely with the Regional Business Director and cross-functional partners to connect customer needs, patient journeys, referral pathways, access dynamics, and business opportunities while demonstrating curiosity, high emotional intelligence, resilience, ownership, and consistent follow-through.

JOB FUNCTIONS/RESPONSIBILITIES

Territory Strategy & Business Performance

  • Develop and execute a focused territory business plan aligned with national, zone, and regional priorities, with clear objectives, customer priorities, resource allocation, and measures of success.
  • Use performance data, customer insights, market intelligence, access dynamics, and competitive trends to identify opportunities, anticipate barriers, and make timely adjustments to territory strategy and execution.
  • Delivers territory business objectives through disciplined prioritization, high-quality customer engagement, effective resource stewardship, and accountability for both behaviors and results.
  • Maintain accurate and timely customer records, forecasts, expense reporting, required administrative documentation, and business updates in accordance with company expectations.

Strategic Account Management & Network Development

  • Identify, prioritize, and develop high-opportunity accounts, health systems, centers of excellence, and referral networks across pediatric and adult hepatology and gastroenterology.
  • Create and execute customized account plans that reflect the local patient journey, key stakeholders, clinical decision-making, referral patterns, access considerations, customer needs, and competitive realities.
  • Build trusted relationships with physicians, advanced practice providers, nurses, pharmacists, office staff, and other members of the care team by delivering relevant value and consistent follow-through.
  • Map influence and decision-making within complex accounts, establish clear objectives for each engagement, and secure appropriate next steps that advance the account strategy.
  • Coordinate compliant account actions across Mirum field partners, clarify ownership, and maintain momentum against agreed priorities and customer needs.

Clinical Aptitude & Customer Engagement

  • Develop and maintain deep knowledge of rare cholestatic liver disease, diagnostic pathways, mechanisms of action, clinical data, product profiles, approved uses, safety information, patient support pathways, access and reimbursement, and the evolving competitive landscape.
  • Communicate complex scientific and clinical information clearly, accurately, and credibly, tailoring the discussion to the knowledge, needs, and priorities of each healthcare professional and account.
  • Engage healthcare professionals as a clinically credible peer by asking insightful questions, listening actively, uncovering unmet needs, and connecting relevant evidence and resources to the customer's practice.
  • Execute approved promotional programs, resources, and customer engagements with consistency, clinical relevance, sound judgment, and full adherence to company policies and regulatory requirements.

Influence & Impact

  • Help customers recognize gaps in disease awareness, patient identification, referral, treatment consideration, and ongoing support by reframing issues and connecting insights across the patient journey.
  • Use high emotional intelligence, curiosity, credibility, and thoughtful questioning to build trust with skeptical, change-resistant, or highly experienced healthcare professionals.
  • Influence multiple stakeholders without authority, navigate resistance constructively, and balance persistence with judgment, empathy, and respect for customer boundaries

Customer, Patient & Caregiver Impact

  • Keep patients and caregivers at the center of territory and account decisions, with a clear understanding of the journey from disease recognition and diagnosis through treatment initiation and persistence.
  • Support a customer experience grounded in trust, empathy, responsiveness, urgency, and reliable follow-through with healthcare professionals and care teams.
  • Collaborate compliantly with Market Access and Patient Services partners to help care teams understand available resources and navigate appropriate barriers in the patient journey.
  • Identify recurring customer, access, and patient-support barriers; elevate them objectively and promptly; and partner with the appropriate internal teams to improve execution and support.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Field Insights

  • Build productive partnerships with Medical Affairs, Market Access, Patient Services, Marketing, Commercial Training and Effectiveness, Operations, Analytics, and Advocacy.
  • Work seamlessly across field roles to coordinate account strategy, align priorities, clarify responsibilities, and ensure consistent follow-through while respecting functional boundaries.
  • Capture and communicate timely, objective, and actionable field insights that can inform strategy, messaging, training, resource development, customer experience, and execution priorities.
  • Contribute actively to business reviews, training programs, team meetings, launch readiness, and cross-functional initiatives; share best practices and support the success of the broader organization.

Entrepreneurial Drive, Resilience & Culture

  • Operate with a high degree of ownership, self-motivation, resourcefulness, and initiative in an unstructured, rapidly evolving rare disease environment.
  • Create appropriate engagement opportunities in underdeveloped accounts and markets, test new approaches, learn quickly, and translate insights into action.
  • Maintain sustained drive, discipline, and performance through pressure, uncertainty, obstacles, delays, and discouragement; recover quickly and remain focused on long-term goals.
  • Demonstrate curiosity, coachability, and a commitment to continuous learning; actively seek feedback and apply coaching to strengthen clinical, strategic, and selling capabilities.
  • Model Mirum's values and the highest standards of ethical conduct, compliance, transparency, inclusion, and respect in every internal and external interaction.

QUALIFICATIONS

Education/Experience:

  • Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree preferred.
  • 5+ years of progressive sales experience in the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry.
  • Demonstrated track record of consistently delivering business results in a complex specialty, rare disease, orphan drug, or high-science market.
  • Rare disease experience is highly preferred; experience in hepatology, gastroenterology, pediatric specialty care, or another complex specialty market is highly desirable.
  • Strong clinical aptitude and demonstrated ability to learn, retain, and communicate complex disease-state, diagnostic, mechanism-of-action, clinical-data, and product information.
  • Experience with account-based selling across health systems, centers of excellence, multidisciplinary care teams, referral networks, and influential healthcare professionals.
  • Demonstrated ability to use insight-led or challenger-style selling to constructively challenge the status quo, influence behavior, and advance customer decision-making.
  • Working knowledge of access and reimbursement dynamics, patient support pathways, and the role of patient services in rare disease markets.
  • Strong business acumen and ability to interpret performance data, identify insights, develop territory and account strategies, and translate plans into consistent field execution.
  • Exceptional interpersonal skills, emotional intelligence, communication, presentation, judgment, and ability to build trust with diverse and highly sophisticated customers.
  • Proven self-motivation, resourcefulness, resilience, organization, and ability to prioritize and perform independently in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment.
  • Demonstrated success partnering cross-functionally with Medical Affairs, Market Access, Patient Services, Marketing, Commercial Training and Effectiveness, Operations, and Analytics.
  • Commitment to ethical conduct, compliance, and approved promotional practices, with sound judgment in complex customer and patient-related situations.
  • Valid driver's license and ability to travel up to 70%, including frequent overnight travel and occasional weekend commitments.

Mirum Pharmaceuticals is committed to Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) and to compliance with all Federal, State and Local laws that prohibit employment discrimination on the basis of race, age, national origin, ethnicity, religion, gender, gender identity, pregnancy, marital status, sexual orientation, citizenship, genetic disposition or characteristics, disability, veteran’s status or any other classification protected by applicable State/Federal/Local laws.

Mirum Pharmaceuticals provides reasonable accommodation for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in job application procedures.

raw.description:
POS-33518

About the Team

Breeze Assistant is HubSpot's AI-powered gateway to value — the conversational front door through which every HubSpot customer starts their work, gets outcomes, and grows with the product. Our mission is to make Breeze the fastest, best way to achieve sales and marketing outcomes in HubSpot: from a new customer's very first session through the seasoned marketer orchestrating complex multi-step GTM workflows.

We significantly increased both CSAT and weekly active penetration by building a foundation-first, tightly-scoped system. We are now running that same playbook at scale — shipping a full agentic platform that every HubSpot team builds on. The next leg of the journey is larger: Breeze becomes the place a customer can get any GTM task done, powered by complete customer context, agentic everboarding, and a platform mature enough that partners and internal teams build their most important use cases on top of it.

If a marketer or seller can get their real work done — and done better — inside Breeze, they stay in HubSpot, come back, and grow. We build so they never have to leave.

About the Role

We are seeking a Principal Software Engineer to be the technical anchor for the Breeze Assistant platform. This role sits at the intersection of robust distributed systems, bleeding-edge Generative AI, and real customer outcomes.

You are not just following a roadmap — you are helping define it. You will shape how Breeze moves from a highly capable assistant to a trusted, proactive agent: one that delivers durable, shareable artifacts grounded in CRM data; dynamically generates the UI a user needs for the task at hand; orchestrates multi-step workflows across HubSpot and third-party tools; and learns from every interaction to get better. The scale is real — millions of users, petabytes of context, and a platform that every HubSpot engineering team depends on.

Key Expectations

  • Agentic Platform Architecture: Define the patterns for how AI agents safely interact with HubSpot's CRM, agentic primitives (skills, tools, memory, scheduled prompts), and third-party ecosystems (Slack, Google Workspace, Gong, etc.). You set the bar for how Breeze orchestrates deterministic and non-deterministic steps — choosing the right blend for trust, cost, and outcome quality.
  • Building Breakthrough Surfaces: Breeze already delivers a significant volume of artifacts across reports, decks, and pages. You will extend the platform so every HubSpot team builds their highest-value deliverables into Breeze — expanding artifact types, opening the platform for internal builders, and driving toward Breeze being the default surface for customers and teams to build on.
  • Complete Customer Context: Work closely with the Context team to ensure every Breeze interaction is powered by complete, trustworthy growth context: company and industry data, outcome history, learning loops, and customer goals. You will build the technical bridges that let context evolve from a data layer into a dynamic, active collaborator in every user's GTM work.
  • Rapid GenAI Experimentation: Act as a zero-to-one builder. You stay current with the latest in LLMs, RAG, and agentic frameworks to rapidly prototype and validate new capabilities — and you know when to ship the prototype and when to wait for production-grade infrastructure.
  • Hands-on, High-Leverage Contributor: You ship production code. You will lead development of high-impact initiatives, moving from a prototype to a production system supporting a broad user base.
  • System Reliability & Trust: Ensure GenAI outputs are not just capable, but trustworthy. You will drive strategy around LLM evaluation, observability, guardrails, and data privacy — the technical foundation that lets customers trust Breeze enough to run real business processes on it.
  • Cross-Functional Technical Leadership: Breeze is both a product and a platform. You will partner with Product, AI Research, HubSpot engineering teams, and the Ecosystem teams to ensure every HubSpot team can expose their tools and API endpoints to Breeze — because coverage is the single biggest unlock for use-case completeness.
  • Technical Mentorship & Multiplier: Elevate AI fluency across the engineering org. Mentor senior engineers on prompt engineering, model selection, agentic design patterns, and the nuances of building non-deterministic systems at scale.

What You Bring

  • Proven Expertise in Distributed Systems: You have built and scaled high-throughput, low-latency systems with strict reliability requirements — the kind that support high concurrency and vast data scale.
  • GenAI Proficiency: Deep experience with LLM orchestration, vector databases, RAG pipelines, and multi-agent frameworks. You understand the trade-offs between model architectures, fine-tuning strategies, and inference costs, and you make principled bets.
  • Agentic System Design: A background in building autonomous or semi-autonomous systems where AI takes actions, handles tool-calling, manages complex state, and recovers gracefully from failure. You've thought hard about the interplay between deterministic and non-deterministic steps in production workflows.
  • Platform Thinking: You build for other builders. You design primitives — skills, tools, APIs, agentic harnesses — that internal teams and partners can compose into use cases you haven't imagined yet.
  • User-First Mindset: You have a track record of building products that people love. You advocate for the end-user in design reviews and understand the pain points of sales and marketing professionals well enough to know when a technical tradeoff harms the outcome.
  • Bias for Action: You prefer a working prototype over a lengthy design doc. You turn ambiguity into clear plans and working software, and you know how to balance the speed of AI experimentation with the rigor of production-grade systems.
  • Rapid Domain Fluency: The AI landscape changes weekly. You dive into a new paper, model, or framework today and can explain its strategic value — and its limitations — to the team tomorrow.

Why This Role, Why Now

Breeze is at an inflection point. The foundation works — CSAT and WAU are both climbing, artifacts are resonating, and the agentic platform is coming online. The next phase is about scale, coverage, and trust: making Breeze the place where every HubSpot customer does their most important work, on a platform mature enough that every Hub team builds their highest-value customer journeys into it.

This Principal Engineer will have a direct line of sight from the architecture they design to the customer outcomes we measure — WAU, CSAT, artifacts opened, credits consumed. If you want to build AI systems that matter at scale, with a team that has already proven the playbook works, this is the role.

Pay & Benefits

The cash compensation below includes base salary, on-target commission for employees in eligible roles, and annual bonus targets under HubSpot’s bonus plan for eligible roles. In addition to cash compensation, some roles are eligible to participate in HubSpot’s equity plan to receive restricted stock units (RSUs). Some roles may also be eligible for overtime pay. Individual compensation packages are tailored to your skills, experience, qualifications, and other job-related reasons.

This resource will help guide how we recommend thinking about the range you see. Learn more about HubSpot’s compensation philosophy.

Benefits are also an important piece of your total compensation package. Explore the benefits and perks HubSpot offers to help employees grow better.

At HubSpot, fair compensation practices aren’t just about checking off the box for legal compliance. It’s about living out our value of transparency with our employees, candidates, and community.

Annual Cash Compensation Range:
$266,200—$425,900 USD

At HubSpot, we value both flexibility and connection. Whether you’re a Remote employee or work from the Office, we want you to start your journey here by building strong connections with your team and peers. If you are joining our Engineering team, you will be required to attend a regional HubSpot office for in-person onboarding. If you join our broader Product team, you’ll also attend other in-person events, such as your Product Group Summit and other gatherings, to continue building on those connections.

About HubSpot

HubSpot (NYSE: HUBS) is an AI-powered customer platform with all the software, integrations, and resources customers need to connect marketing, sales, and service. HubSpot's connected platform enables businesses to grow faster by focusing on what matters most: customers.

At HubSpot, bold is our baseline. Our employees around the globe move fast, stay customer-obsessed, and win together. Our culture is grounded in four commitments: Solve for the Customer, Be Bold, Learn Fast, Align, Adapt & Go!, and Deliver with HEART. These commitments shape how we work, lead, and grow.

We’re building a company where people can do their best work. We focus on brilliant work, not badge swipes. By combining clarity, ownership, and trust, we create space for big thinking and meaningful progress. And we know that when our employees grow, our customers do too.

Recognized globally for our award-winning culture by Comparably, Glassdoor, Fortune, and more, HubSpot is headquartered in Cambridge, MA, with employees and offices around the world.
